source: Original Obsidian notes and documented primary design references
scope: Web and interface aesthetics, visual composition, typography, and relevant art influences

styles.name: Web Brutalism
styles.description: Raw page structure, blunt typography and exposed browser conventions turn a website's construction into its visual identity.

styles.name: Neubrutalism
styles.description: Strong outlines, hard offset shadows and assertive typography make flat interface elements feel deliberately solid and graphic.

sources.title: Neobrutalism components — bold borders and hard shadows

styles.name: Anti-design
styles.description: Clashing scales, awkward alignment and deliberate visual disruption challenge the polished conventions of commercial websites.

sources.title: AIGA Eye on Design — The Era of Rebellious Web Design

styles.name: Net Art
styles.description: The browser, its windows, links and technical behavior become the material of an artwork and the structure of its interface.

sources.title: Rhizome — One Terabyte of Kilobyte Age

styles.name: GeoCities Web
styles.description: Tiled backgrounds, animated graphics and dense personal collections recreate the handmade visual culture of early homepages.

sources.title: Cameron's World — a GeoCities web collage

styles.name: Flash-era Web
styles.description: Choreographed transitions, sound-led sequences and compact animated worlds give navigation the feel of an interactive title sequence.

sources.title: Web Design Museum — historical website gallery

styles.name: Immersive 3D Web
styles.description: A navigable three-dimensional environment organizes the page, making camera position, lighting and spatial scale part of the interface.

sources.title: Codrops — Windland: An Immersive Three.js Experience

styles.name: Holographic Spatial UI
styles.description: Translucent instruments and luminous control surfaces float in depth, forming layered interfaces around a scene or object.

sources.title: Territory Studio — Pacific Rim: Uprising holographic controls

styles.name: Flat Design
styles.description: Solid shapes and simplified graphics establish hierarchy without simulated lighting or material depth.
styles.distinction: Flatness concerns visual treatment; a flat interface can still contain substantial information.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group — Flat design and Flat 2.0

styles.name: Flat 2.0
styles.description: Mostly flat graphics gain selective shadows and depth cues that make interaction and layering clearer.
styles.distinction: Retains a flat base while restoring limited dimensional signifiers.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group — Flat design and Flat 2.0

styles.name: Skeuomorphism
styles.description: Controls and containers borrow the appearance and familiar behavior of physical objects.
styles.distinction: The physical resemblance carries a functional metaphor, beyond visual texture alone.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group — Flat design and Flat 2.0
Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Material Realism
styles.description: Realistic textures, lighting, and rendered materials give a screen the appearance of physical surfaces.
styles.distinction: Material realism may be purely visual; it does not require a skeuomorphic interaction metaphor.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group — Flat design and Flat 2.0

styles.name: Neumorphism
styles.description: Paired light and dark shadows make controls appear molded from the same material as their background.
styles.distinction: Forms emerge from a continuous surface instead of floating on separate layers.

sources.title: Michał Malewicz — Neumorphism in user interfaces

styles.name: Glassmorphism
styles.description: Translucent, blurred panels and highlighted edges separate interface layers like frosted glass.
styles.distinction: Background visibility and blur define the material, unlike opaque soft shadows.

styles.name: Claymorphism
styles.description: Rounded, inflated forms and soft directional shading give interface objects a clay-like volume.
styles.distinction: Puffy objects remain distinct from the background, unlike molded neumorphic surfaces.

sources.title: Michał Malewicz — Claymorphism in user interfaces

styles.name: Minimalism
styles.description: A limited set of elements, generous open space, and deliberate hierarchy keep attention on essential content.
styles.distinction: Reduction governs the whole page, independent of whether its surfaces are flat or dimensional.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group — The characteristics of minimalism in web design

styles.name: Organic Design
styles.description: Irregular contours, fluid image boundaries, and natural forms soften rigid screen geometry.
styles.distinction: Shape construction defines the direction; changing a conventional interface to green does not.

sources.title: University of Wisconsin — Graphic design: layout and composition
Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Hand-Drawn Design
styles.description: Drawn lines, informal lettering, and intentionally uneven graphic elements give the interface a handmade character.
styles.distinction: The drawn treatment extends across the visual system rather than appearing in one decorative illustration.

sources.title: Adrian Bece — Claymorphism and illustration on the web
Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Duotone
styles.description: Two coordinated tones map an image's shadows and highlights, unifying photography and surrounding graphics.
styles.distinction: A tonal image treatment, distinct from simply using two flat colors in a layout.

styles.name: Warm Minimalism
styles.description: Spare compositions pair natural hues, soft neutrals, and tactile imagery with quiet typography.
styles.distinction: Adds natural material cues and softer contrast to minimalism, rather than merely recoloring a dense composition.

styles.name: Maximalism
styles.description: Dense imagery, ornament, contrasting type, and layered patterns turn visual abundance into a deliberate composition.
styles.distinction: A broad approach to density and eclecticism; it does not require a particular historical motif.

styles.name: Corporate Memphis
styles.description: Friendly, simplified figures and elastic proportions combine with flat shapes and approachable commercial color.
styles.distinction: A recent corporate illustration vernacular, distinct from the patterned objects of the original Memphis group.

styles.name: Vectordelia
styles.description: Crisp vector silhouettes, exuberant flourishes, gradients, stars, and overlapping shapes create expansive digital ornament.
styles.distinction: Also called Frutiger Metro; flatter and more ornamental than Frutiger Aero's photographic gloss.

styles.name: Vectorgarden
styles.description: Botanical vector flourishes, butterflies, translucent curls, and luminous gradients create a delicate digital garden.
styles.distinction: A nature-focused branch of vector ornament, distinguished from Vectordelia's music, urban silhouettes, and denser graphic bursts.

styles.name: Technozen
styles.description: Clean white surfaces, gentle curves, small friendly symbols, and restrained natural accents suggest calm everyday technology.
styles.distinction: A retrospective look associated with 2000s Japanese consumer technology; quieter and less scenic than Frutiger Aero.

styles.name: Synthwave
styles.description: Neon horizons, receding grids, chrome lettering, and sunset gradients reimagine 1980s electronic futurism.
styles.distinction: Builds an idealized cinematic night world; Vaporwave more often remixes consumer imagery and obsolete media.

styles.name: Cyberpunk
styles.description: Dense neon signage, dark industrial surfaces, electronic overlays, and visible urban wear suggest a contested technological future.
styles.distinction: Combines advanced technology with social friction and decay, rather than treating luminous technology as automatically optimistic.

sources.title: Linearity — Cyberpunk: how to master the futuristic style

styles.name: Hyperpop
styles.description: Artificial gloss, exaggerated typography, colliding digital textures, and saturated imagery create a knowingly excessive pop surface.
styles.distinction: Draws on music's synthetic intensity and pop spectacle; distinct from McBling's celebrity luxury motifs.

styles.name: Solarpunk
styles.description: Lush vegetation, organic ornament, and visible renewable technology imagine a cooperative ecological future.
styles.distinction: Nature and technology are presented as a social vision, not simply a green palette or decorative leaves.

sources.title: ACMI — An introduction to solarpunk on screen

styles.name: Frasurbane
styles.description: Classical serif type, sepia imagery, textured paper, and cultivated scientific motifs create a quietly sophisticated 1990s mood.
styles.distinction: Its bookish adult consumer tone differs from Global Village Coffeehouse's rough folk illustration.

styles.name: Global Village Coffeehouse
styles.description: Rough woodcut-like lines, earthy colors, spirals, suns, hands, and organic emblems create a warm commercial folk vernacular.
styles.distinction: Uses irregular symbolic illustration and historically borrowed cultural motifs, rather than Frasurbane's polished classical imagery.

styles.name: Corporate Grunge
styles.description: Distressed type, rough textures, tilted fragments, and compressed layouts bring 1990s alternative graphics into advertising.
styles.distinction: A commercial adaptation of grunge's visual roughness, distinct from punk's original cut-and-paste counterculture.

styles.name: Corporate Hippie
styles.description: Bright, curving illustration and playful psychedelic ornament translate counterculture imagery into approachable commercial graphics.
styles.distinction: The consumer-facing adaptation is more controlled and welcoming than immersive psychedelic visual overload.

styles.name: Utopian Scholastic
styles.description: Classical serif typography, specimen-like objects, and clean photographic collage frame knowledge as inviting and universal.
styles.distinction: Also known as Encartacore; educational image assemblages distinguish it from Frasurbane's lifestyle sophistication.

styles.name: Factory Pomo
styles.description: Industrial signs, constructed geometry, strong diagonals, and machine-age references combine with playful postmodern arrangement.
styles.distinction: Uses early industrial graphic vernacular within late-1980s postmodern design, rather than repeating historical Constructivism.

styles.name: Whimsigothic
styles.description: Celestial emblems, curling shapes, dark jewel tones, and eccentric ornament make gothic imagery playful and dreamlike.
styles.distinction: Combines whimsy with gothic theatricality; unlike ordinary goth styling, its forms often feel storybook-like.

styles.name: Whimsicraft
styles.description: Colorful folk shapes, found-object collage, visible joins, and handmade textures celebrate playful assembly.
styles.distinction: The craft revival's assembled material character differs from flat whimsical illustration.

styles.name: Hipness Purgatory
styles.description: Loose hand lettering, offbeat drawings, mundane objects, and knowingly awkward retro cues create a twee indie vernacular.
styles.distinction: Associated with 2000s indie consumer culture; its deadpan everyday humor differs from expansive craft ornament.

styles.name: Dollar Store Vernacular
styles.description: Mixed display fonts, clip art, bright gradients, crowded badges, and improvised arrangements create an exuberant everyday commercial look.
styles.distinction: A vernacular of low-budget production and improvised software use, rather than a single intentional design movement.

styles.name: Supergraphic Ultramodern
styles.description: Oversized geometric stripes, rounded futuristic forms, rainbow bands, and confident sans-serif type create a playful synthetic future.
styles.distinction: Its 1960s–1970s supergraphic scale and plastic-age optimism precede Y2K's digital chrome.

styles.name: Steampunk
styles.description: Engraved ornament, brass-like surfaces, mechanical diagrams, and Victorian lettering imagine an alternate industrial technology.
styles.distinction: A speculative historical aesthetic, distinct from actual Victorian graphic artifacts or generic metallic rendering.

styles.name: Swiss International Style
styles.description: Rational grids, sans-serif type, asymmetrical balance, and measured open space form a precise graphic language.
styles.distinction: Unifies the duplicate labels Swiss Style and International Typographic Style.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: New Typography
styles.description: Functional hierarchy, asymmetry, and modern lettering organize the page as active visual communication.
styles.distinction: An earlier modernist typographic approach, broader than the later Swiss system.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes
University of Wisconsin — Graphic design: layout and composition

styles.name: Column Grid
styles.description: Continuous vertical alignments organize images and text into a stable, readable page structure.
styles.distinction: Columns align content vertically without requiring a repeated horizontal module.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group — Using grids in interface designs

styles.name: Modular Grid
styles.description: Repeated columns and rows establish regular cells for images, text, and interface elements.
styles.distinction: Adds horizontal modules to a column grid; not every module becomes an individual card.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group — Using grids in interface designs

styles.name: Hierarchical Grid
styles.description: Unequal regions give major content greater space while arranging supporting material around it.
styles.distinction: Allocates area by importance rather than maintaining uniformly sized modules.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group — Using grids in interface designs

styles.name: Bento Grid
styles.description: A compact arrangement of differently sized, self-contained panels presents varied content as one composition.
styles.distinction: Compartmentalized panels distinguish it from an open hierarchical editorial grid.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes
Nielsen Norman Group — Cards: UI-component definition

styles.name: Card-Based Design
styles.description: Consistent containers gather related images and information into distinct, repeatable visual units.
styles.distinction: Cards define content units; their arrangement need not be bento-shaped or masonry-packed.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group — Cards: UI-component definition

styles.name: Masonry Layout
styles.description: Uneven-height blocks pack into continuous columns, making image proportions shape the page.
styles.distinction: Vertical packing differs from equal-height rows in a justified gallery.

styles.name: Justified Image Grid
styles.description: Rows of images share a height while retaining varied widths, filling the available horizontal space.
styles.distinction: Images preserve their aspect ratios within fitted rows, unlike fixed-size contact sheets.

styles.name: Split-Screen Layout
styles.description: Two prominent panels share the viewport, creating a sustained relationship between parallel visual streams.
styles.distinction: A deliberate two-part page structure rather than ordinary multi-column text.

sources.title: AIGA Eye on Design — Digital magazines and reading conventions
Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Asymmetric Layout
styles.description: Unequal visual masses and open space create balance without a centered or mirrored arrangement.
styles.distinction: Balance comes from visual weight rather than an evenly divided split screen.

sources.title: University of Wisconsin — Graphic design: layout and composition
Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Editorial Design
styles.description: Expressive headlines, varied image scales, and carefully paced reading blocks borrow the rhythm of print publications.
styles.distinction: A broad art-directed reading language, not a requirement for dense newspaper columns.

sources.title: Andy Clarke — Inspired Design Decisions: Ernest Journal
Andy Clarke — Inspired Design Decisions: Avaunt Magazine

styles.name: Newspaper Design
styles.description: Ruled columns, compact headlines, and a clear hierarchy of stories create a dense, browsable reading field.
styles.distinction: More tightly structured and information-dense than the broader editorial direction.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group — Using grids in interface designs

styles.name: Book Design
styles.description: Facing-page relationships pair images and text across the screen, treating the viewport as a reading spread.
styles.distinction: Uses the relationship between facing pages rather than a generic two-panel tool.

sources.title: AIGA Eye on Design — Digital magazines and reading conventions
Andy Clarke — Inspired Design Decisions: Ernest Journal

styles.name: Marginalia
styles.description: A primary reading column is accompanied by small annotations, captions, or contextual notes in generous margins.
styles.distinction: Peripheral commentary becomes part of the page language, not an ordinary navigation sidebar.

sources.title: Andy Clarke — Inspired Design Decisions: Ernest Journal
Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Full-Bleed Composition
styles.description: Large images reach the edges of the viewing area, with typography placed around or across the imagery.
styles.distinction: Image fields define the screen rather than appearing inside repeated framed cards.

sources.title: Andy Clarke — Inspired Design Decisions: Avaunt Magazine
Andy Clarke — Inspired Design Decisions: Ernest Journal

styles.name: Framed Composition
styles.description: Generous borders and deliberate margins present images as individual objects within a restrained page.
styles.distinction: The surrounding frame and space remain visible, unlike full-bleed imagery.

sources.title: Andy Clarke — Inspired Design Decisions: Ernest Journal

styles.name: Typographic Index
styles.description: Names, numbers, and short metadata form a compact, predominantly textual visual catalogue.
styles.distinction: The index itself is the main composition, rather than an incidental menu.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Contact Sheet
styles.description: Uniform image cells, consistent captions, and repeated numbering make a collection read as a visual archive.
styles.distinction: Uniformity and cataloguing distinguish it from varied masonry or bento panels.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group — Using grids in interface designs
Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Overlapping Layout
styles.description: Images and type deliberately cross one another’s boundaries, making layered relationships visible.
styles.distinction: Overlap is the dominant organizing device; freeform placement alone need not overlap.

sources.title: Andy Clarke — Inspired Design Decisions: Avaunt Magazine

styles.name: Freeform Layout
styles.description: Elements are positioned as a graphic field, with scale and visual balance taking precedence over repeated rows.
styles.distinction: A composed spatial arrangement, distinct from random placement or algorithmic generation.

styles.name: Diagonal Composition
styles.description: Slanted alignments and directional image relationships lead the eye across the page.
styles.distinction: Direction is established by the composition rather than by italic lettering alone.

sources.title: University of Wisconsin — Graphic design: layout and composition
Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Radial Composition
styles.description: Elements gather around a center, using circular relationships and spokes to establish hierarchy.
styles.distinction: A center-out structure differs from linear columns or a freeform image field.

sources.title: University of Wisconsin — Graphic design: layout and composition

styles.name: Tabular Design
styles.description: Aligned rows, compact labels, and repeated data columns create an orderly, information-dense visual field.
styles.distinction: Tables and alignment dominate the appearance, not merely the presence of a chart.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes
Nielsen Norman Group — Using grids in interface designs

styles.name: Cartographic Design
styles.description: Map fields, location marks, routes, and geographic labels organize a spatially grounded interface.
styles.distinction: Geographic position determines composition; a node graph may have no geographic meaning.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Node-Link Diagram
styles.description: Connected nodes and labeled relationships turn the screen into a readable network of entities.
styles.distinction: Connections determine the visible structure rather than a general infinite canvas.

styles.name: Schematic Design
styles.description: Fine lines, measured labels, and diagrammatic views give the interface the clarity of a technical drawing.
styles.distinction: Explains structure through diagrams rather than simulating a fictional HUD.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes
University of Wisconsin — Graphic design: layout and composition

styles.name: Pictographic Design
styles.description: Repeated symbols and clear groupings communicate information through recognizable visual units.
styles.distinction: Pictograms carry the information itself, beyond decorative icons beside text.

sources.title: University of Wisconsin — Graphic design: layout and composition

styles.name: Treemap
styles.description: Nested rectangles of varying area display hierarchy as a continuous, space-filling graphic field.
styles.distinction: Area represents a hierarchy or quantity, unlike decorative bento compartments.

styles.name: Small Multiples
styles.description: Repeated visual panels use a consistent scale and structure to make differences easy to compare.
styles.distinction: The repeated comparison system defines the view, rather than unrelated cards.

styles.name: Photomontage
styles.description: Cut, combined, and rescaled photographs construct a new scene, argument, or impossible relationship.
styles.distinction: Photographic source fragments are essential; this differs from collage built mainly from paper, lettering, or found objects.

styles.name: Geometric sans-serif typography
styles.description: Circular bowls, simple construction, and repeated shapes give type-led pages a geometric rhythm.
styles.distinction: Constructed geometry differs from the calligraphic proportions of humanist sans.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Grotesque typography
styles.description: Early sans-serif irregularities, uneven stroke contrast, and blunt forms give headlines a workmanlike character.
styles.distinction: Retains eccentric forms that neo-grotesques regularize.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Neo-grotesque typography
styles.description: Regular sans-serif shapes and coordinated weights organize interfaces through quiet, consistent type.
styles.distinction: More systematic and neutral than early grotesques; not synonymous with a complete Swiss layout.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Humanist sans-serif typography
styles.description: Open counters and writing-derived proportions give interface text a warmer, more varied rhythm.
styles.distinction: Calligraphic structure distinguishes it from geometric and neo-grotesque type.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Rounded sans-serif typography
styles.description: Rounded terminals and soft corners make type the gentle, tactile center of a visual system.
styles.distinction: Rounding changes the stroke endings, not just the color or weight of a geometric font.

styles.name: Superellipse typography
styles.description: Squared curves and rounded rectangular counters produce a technical, compact lettering language.
styles.distinction: Superelliptical bowls differ from circular geometric construction.

styles.name: Humanist serif typography
styles.description: Broad-pen influence, angled stress, and softly bracketed serifs give reading pages a manuscript-derived character.
styles.distinction: Earlier and more visibly calligraphic than refined Garalde forms.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Garalde typography
styles.description: Refined old-style serifs, moderate contrast, and sloping stress give editorial screens a bookish texture.
styles.distinction: More regular and refined than Venetian humanist serifs, with less vertical stress than transitional faces.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Transitional serif typography
styles.description: Sharper contrast and increasingly vertical stress balance traditional reading texture with precise detail.
styles.distinction: Bridges old-style serifs and the more extreme contrast of Didones.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Didone typography
styles.description: Hairline serifs and emphatic thick–thin contrast make large editorial headings crisp and dramatic.
styles.distinction: Vertical contrast and unbracketed fine serifs distinguish it from transitional type.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Fat-face typography
styles.description: Extremely heavy vertical strokes and delicate hairlines turn serif lettering into bold graphic masses.
styles.distinction: A display construction with exaggerated weight contrast, rather than simply bold body text.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Scotch Roman typography
styles.description: Sturdy vertical strokes, bracketed serifs, and strong contrast bring a compact editorial authority.
styles.distinction: Bracketing and robust text forms distinguish Scotch Romans from hairline Didones.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Geometric slab-serif typography
styles.description: Geometric letterforms and rectangular, unbracketed serifs give pages an engineered, sturdy voice.
styles.distinction: Squared mechanical slabs differ from the curved brackets of Clarendon.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Humanist slab-serif typography
styles.description: Calligraphic proportions combine with substantial serifs for a sturdy but approachable reading texture.
styles.distinction: Uses humanist rather than geometric construction beneath the slab serifs.

styles.name: Clarendon typography
styles.description: Bracketed slab serifs and compact, weighty letters create a firm display rhythm.
styles.distinction: Rounded brackets separate this language from unbracketed Egyptian slabs.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Glyphic typography
styles.description: Chiseled terminals and inscription-like proportions give type-led screens a monumental restraint.
styles.distinction: Its forms derive from carved lettering rather than pen-written serifs.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Blackletter typography
styles.description: Dense, angular strokes and fractured curves make lettering an emphatic ornamental presence.
styles.distinction: A manuscript-derived construction, distinct from ordinary condensed serif type.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Formal script typography
styles.description: Connected, sloping letterforms and controlled flourishes give display text a penmanship-led elegance.
styles.distinction: Regular formal writing differs from loose brush and casual handwritten lettering.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Brush-script typography
styles.description: Visible brush pressure, energetic joins, and varying stroke width make headings feel painted.
styles.distinction: Brush-shaped strokes distinguish it from formal pointed-pen scripts.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Handwritten typography
styles.description: Personal letter variation and informal spacing give interfaces the intimacy of written notes.
styles.distinction: Emphasizes irregular everyday writing instead of formal script conventions.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Upright script typography
styles.description: Connected cursive forms stay comparatively upright, combining flowing joins with a steady vertical rhythm.
styles.distinction: Connectivity is retained without the strong slant common to formal scripts.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Stencil typography
styles.description: Interrupted strokes and visible bridges turn lettering into a cut, fabricated graphic system.
styles.distinction: The bridges are structural features of the letters, not a distressed texture.

styles.name: Wood-type typography
styles.description: Heavy display letters, varied widths, and nineteenth-century printing character give headings a tactile presence.
styles.distinction: Draws on wood display type rather than a generic old-fashioned serif.

sources.title: Type Network — Adobe Originals: Wood Type Revival

styles.name: Tuscan typography
styles.description: Split or ornamental serifs and decorated letter structures give display text an elaborate sign-like character.
styles.distinction: Ornament changes the letter anatomy, beyond a standard slab serif.

sources.title: Type Network — Adobe Originals: Wood Type Revival

styles.name: Inline typography
styles.description: Fine interior strokes travel through bold letters, creating a decorative second contour.
styles.distinction: Interior lines remain inside filled letterforms; outline typography removes the fill.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Outline typography
styles.description: Hollow letterforms let background space pass through large headings and typographic images.
styles.distinction: The letter is drawn by its boundary, unlike the interior decoration of inline type.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes
Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Shadow typography
styles.description: Letterforms carry drawn offset or dimensional shadows, giving display text a graphic sense of depth.
styles.distinction: Depth belongs to the type itself; the surrounding interface can remain flat.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes
Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Chromatic typography
styles.description: Coordinated letter layers create multicolor forms and printed dimensional effects.
styles.distinction: Layered type construction, rather than ordinary letters assigned different colors.

sources.title: Type Network — Adobe Originals: Wood Type Revival
Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Condensed typography
styles.description: Narrow letterforms create dense vertical rhythms and headlines that pack tightly across a screen.
styles.distinction: Width is a dominant compositional feature; not equivalent to small or condensed body copy.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Extended typography
styles.description: Wide letterforms stretch headlines into horizontal bands and emphasize the width of the page.
styles.distinction: Expansion changes letter proportions rather than merely adding tracking.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Reverse-contrast typography
styles.description: Heavy horizontal strokes and lighter verticals invert familiar letter weight, producing an unconventional display voice.
styles.distinction: The direction of stroke contrast changes, beyond ordinary boldness.

sources.title: Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Modular typography
styles.description: Repeated geometric units construct letters and connect type with the surrounding graphic system.
styles.distinction: Letters are assembled from shared modules rather than simply drawn with geometric proportions.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Oversized typography
styles.description: Very large words act as the page’s main visual shapes, with scale establishing hierarchy.
styles.distinction: A composition-led direction that can use many typeface classes.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Type-specimen design
styles.description: Glyph samples, weight comparisons, and carefully staged text turn typography itself into the visual subject.
styles.distinction: Centers on displaying the type system, rather than using a large headline alone.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Mincho typography
styles.description: Contrasting strokes and triangular terminals give Japanese text a precise, print-derived rhythm.
styles.distinction: A specific Japanese classification; not a synonym for every serif style in East Asian scripts.

sources.title: Google Fonts Knowledge — Japanese type classification
Google Fonts — The Zen Fonts collection

styles.name: Kaku Gothic typography
styles.description: Even strokes and squared endings give Japanese text a clear, structured sans-serif appearance.
styles.distinction: Angular endings distinguish it from rounded Maru Gothic.

sources.title: Google Fonts Knowledge — Japanese type classification
Google Fonts — The Zen Fonts collection

styles.name: Maru Gothic typography
styles.description: Rounded stroke ends soften Japanese sans-serif forms into a friendly, open text texture.
styles.distinction: A rounded Japanese classification, distinct from Kaku Gothic.

sources.title: Google Fonts Knowledge — Japanese type classification
Google Fonts — The Zen Fonts collection

styles.name: Naskh typography
styles.description: Flowing Arabic-script joins and balanced letter proportions create a legible, calligraphic reading texture.
styles.distinction: Uses continuous cursive structure rather than the more geometric rhythm associated with Kufic designs.

sources.title: 29LT — Arabic type anatomy and typographic terms
W3C Internationalization — Typeface styles and font fallback

styles.name: Kufic-inspired typography
styles.description: Geometric construction and emphatic horizontal and vertical relationships structure Arabic-script display text.
styles.distinction: A broad family with historical variations; contemporary geometric interpretations are not all identical to early Kufic.

sources.title: 29LT — Arabic type anatomy and typographic terms

styles.name: Nastaliq typography
styles.description: Sloping word groups and intricate stacked relationships give Urdu and Persian text a distinctive flowing rhythm.
styles.distinction: Word-level diagonal structure differs from Naskh’s more horizontal text line.

sources.title: W3C Internationalization — Typeface styles and font fallback

styles.name: Ruq’ah typography
styles.description: Compact forms, clipped letters, and simple curves produce a brisk handwritten Arabic-script texture.
styles.distinction: Short forms and a steadier line distinguish it from elaborate Nastaliq and fully formed Naskh.

sources.title: W3C Internationalization — Typeface styles and font fallback

styles.name: Vertical Japanese typography
styles.description: Vertical text columns and carefully oriented punctuation turn reading direction into the organizing graphic structure.
styles.distinction: A writing and composition direction, independent of whether the type is Mincho or Gothic.

sources.title: Google Fonts Knowledge — Japanese type classification
Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Monospaced editorial typography
styles.description: Equal-width characters establish a measured text rhythm across headings, captions, and editorial layouts.
styles.distinction: Typography-led pages need not imitate a terminal or historical computer screen.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes

styles.name: Distressed typography
styles.description: Eroded edges and uneven printed marks make display letters feel worn and materially imperfect.
styles.distinction: Texture is built into the lettering; it does not require an entire grunge or punk composition.

sources.title: Type Network — Adobe Originals: Wood Type Revival

styles.name: Sign-painted lettering
styles.description: Brush-built letters, custom joins, outlines, and drawn shadows bring the character of painted signs to screens.
styles.distinction: A lettering craft with deliberate construction, distinct from casual handwritten text.

sources.title: Hamanti — Original Obsidian typography and composition notes
Monotype — A guide to type styles

styles.name: Terminal UI
styles.description: Monospaced text, command prompts and a restrained screen palette give the page the direct visual logic of a command line.

styles.name: Text-mode UI
styles.description: Character-drawn borders, text menus and rectangular panels organize information as a complete graphical layout made from type.

styles.name: Classic Macintosh UI
styles.description: Compact bitmap icons, striped title bars and sharply outlined windows establish a crisp monochrome desktop language.

styles.name: Windows 95 UI
styles.description: Beveled gray controls, inset fields and compact title bars make the page resemble a tactile desktop assembled from rectangular modules.

styles.name: Windows XP Luna
styles.description: Rounded window chrome, glossy controls and strongly separated colored title bars bring an approachable consumer-software character to interfaces.

styles.name: Mac OS X Aqua
styles.description: Translucent gel-like controls, polished gradients and softly shaded panels give the desktop the appearance of luminous physical objects.

styles.name: Windows Aero UI
styles.description: Transparent window frames, soft reflections and illuminated controls layer the desktop behind a glass-like interface shell.

styles.name: BeOS UI
styles.description: Short tab-shaped title bars, crisp beveled controls and detailed compact icons create a distinctive modular desktop rhythm.

styles.name: NeXTSTEP UI
styles.description: Dark beveled title bars, square dock tiles and restrained grayscale surfaces give desktop controls a dense workstation character.

styles.name: Amiga Workbench UI
styles.description: Angular bitmap controls, compact iconography and sharply segmented window furniture reflect the visual economy of early multimedia desktops.

styles.name: ANSI Art
styles.description: Colored character blocks and box-drawing symbols form dense illustrations, lettering and menus within a fixed text grid.

sources.title: Sixteen Colors — ANSI and ASCII art archive

styles.name: Teletext Art
styles.description: Large mosaic cells, limited colors and rigid character grids turn screen constraints into bold geometric pictures and text.

sources.title: Dragan Espenschied — teletext and web art

styles.name: Winamp Skinning
styles.description: Custom bitmap panels, miniature instruments and heavily styled controls transform a media-player window into a compact graphic object.

sources.title: Skin Museum — history of Winamp skins

styles.name: CRT Display
styles.description: Scan lines, phosphor glow and visible color cells give digital content the luminous texture of a cathode-ray screen.

sources.title: Maxime Heckel — The Art of Dithering and Retro Shading for the Web

styles.name: Y2K Futurism
styles.description: Chrome surfaces, translucent plastics and streamlined digital forms express the technological optimism surrounding the turn of the millennium.

styles.name: Metalheart
styles.description: Intricate abstract three-dimensional structures, layered technical marks and compressed detail create a dense technological image.

styles.name: Vectorheart
styles.description: Sharp vector forms, industrial symbols and forceful typography create a fast, highly organized version of millennial futurism.

styles.name: Corporate Cyberspace
styles.description: Layered photographs, motion blur and experimental type translate early digital culture into energetic commercial graphics.

styles.name: Gen X Soft Club
styles.description: Muted urban imagery, natural textures and restrained modern type combine a minimal graphic structure with an understated organic mood.

styles.name: Frutiger Aero
styles.description: Glossy interface imagery joins bright skies, water and greenery in an optimistic vision of technology integrated with nature.

styles.name: Acidgrafix
styles.description: Distorted lettering, chrome forms and unusual textures fill compositions with deliberately unstable, densely layered visual energy.

styles.name: Hexatron
styles.description: Angular technology, hexagonal grids and luminous instrumentation create a sharply segmented science-fiction visual language.

styles.name: Cyberbougie
styles.description: Dark surfaces, monospaced details and luminous gradients give technology branding a sleek, computational character.

styles.name: Blob World
styles.description: Elaborate soft-body renders and uncanny textures arrange playful objects into surreal three-dimensional compositions.

styles.name: McBling
styles.description: Rhinestones, metallic shine and conspicuous decorative excess turn early-2000s consumer imagery into a maximal graphic surface.

styles.name: Cyberdelia
styles.description: Fractal forms, kaleidoscopic color and early computer graphics combine electronic technology with psychedelic imagery.

styles.name: Early Cyber
styles.description: Rough pixel imagery, digitally warped lettering and desktop-publishing experiments expose the first wave of computer-generated graphic expression.

styles.name: Silicon Dreams
styles.description: Surreal spaces, primitive geometric objects and conspicuous computer rendering recall the visual imagination of early 3D animation.

styles.name: Laser Grid
styles.description: Perspective grids, glowing lines and reflective surfaces turn 1980s high-technology imagery into a structured futuristic stage.

styles.name: Vaporwave
styles.description: Outdated consumer graphics, early digital imagery and displaced cultural fragments create an uneasy nostalgia for commercial futures.

sources.title: Xiaolong Zhang — What is visual Vaporwave?

styles.name: Webcore
styles.description: Old browser windows, error messages and pixel graphics are remixed into surreal scenes rooted in early internet experience.

styles.name: Weirdcore
styles.description: Familiar low-fidelity images and disorienting text are combined to make ordinary digital spaces feel inexplicably unsettling.

sources.title: Lampoon — Internet aesthetics, Weirdcore and Dreamcore

styles.name: Dreamcore
styles.description: Soft, dreamlike imagery and improbable spaces form a nostalgic visual world that follows emotional association over physical logic.

sources.title: Lampoon — Internet aesthetics, Weirdcore and Dreamcore

styles.name: Cybersigilism
styles.description: Spiked, branching linework fuses symbol-like forms with a digital sensibility, often becoming graphic emblems or ornamental interfaces.

styles.name: Cassette Futurism
styles.description: Bulky controls, angular hardware and analog display cues imagine advanced technology through the physical language of 1970s and 1980s equipment.

styles.name: Fictional User Interface
styles.description: Dense readouts, diagrams and animated instruments give invented technology a coherent visual system for a fictional world.

styles.name: Voxel Art
styles.description: Visible cubic units build objects and scenes, giving three-dimensional imagery the ordered block structure of a pixel grid.

sources.title: Codrops — Turning 3D Models to Voxel Art with Three.js

styles.name: Low-poly Rendering
styles.description: A small number of visible facets simplifies objects into angular silhouettes and broad planes of light.

sources.title: Codrops — Windland: An Immersive Three.js Experience

styles.name: PS1-era 3D
styles.description: Low-resolution textures, unstable polygon edges and coarse shading reproduce the characteristic visual limitations of early console rendering.

styles.name: Cel Shading
styles.description: Discrete bands of light and shadow flatten three-dimensional forms into a graphic image resembling painted animation cels.

styles.name: Wireframe Rendering
styles.description: Visible mesh edges describe form while leaving surfaces open, emphasizing digital construction and geometric structure.

styles.name: Point-cloud Rendering
styles.description: Dense collections of isolated points suggest surfaces and volumes, allowing objects to appear scanned, particulate or partially reconstructed.

styles.name: Gaussian Splatting
styles.description: Overlapping soft volumetric samples reconstruct photographed scenes with an unusually immediate, spatial photographic appearance.

sources.title: Codrops — 3D Glass Portal with Gaussian Splatting

styles.name: Photogrammetry
styles.description: Photographic detail is mapped onto reconstructed three-dimensional forms, retaining surface irregularities and the texture of real objects.

sources.title: Codrops — Blender and photogrammetry case studies

styles.name: Photorealistic 3D
styles.description: Physically based materials and plausible lighting make rendered objects read as photographed surfaces rather than illustrated forms.

styles.name: Chrome Rendering
styles.description: Highly reflective metallic surfaces bend their surroundings into bright highlights and dark contours, emphasizing an object's liquid or sculptural shape.

styles.name: Holographic Graphics
styles.description: Luminous lines, transparent layers and projected volumes make information appear suspended in space rather than printed on a surface.

styles.name: Isometric Rendering
styles.description: Parallel projection presents objects at a consistent angle, creating orderly scenes whose scale remains legible across depth.

styles.name: Anaglyph Graphics
styles.description: Offset color-channel views suggest stereoscopic depth and give edges a deliberately doubled, optically unstable appearance.

styles.name: Matcap Rendering
styles.description: A material-capture texture gives simple geometry a coherent sculptural surface, emphasizing form through stylized highlights and shading.

styles.name: Line-rendered 3D
styles.description: Contours and selected mesh edges replace realistic shading, translating modeled objects into technical or hand-drawn-looking line images.

styles.name: Volumetric Rendering
styles.description: Visible light, fog and semi-transparent density make space itself appear tangible, producing atmospheric depth around objects and type.

styles.name: ASCII Rendering
styles.description: Letters and punctuation replace pixels, describing light and detail through the density of a fixed character grid.

sources.title: Codrops — Efecto: ASCII and Dithering with WebGL

styles.name: Pixel Art
styles.description: Deliberately arranged pixel clusters and limited palettes make each small unit of an image part of its visible construction.

sources.title: Maxime Heckel — The Art of Dithering and Retro Shading for the Web

styles.name: Dithered Rendering
styles.description: Patterns of contrasting pixels simulate intermediate tones, producing a granular surface with a deliberately restricted color range.

sources.title: Maxime Heckel — The Art of Dithering and Retro Shading for the Web

styles.name: Glitch Art
styles.description: Visible failures in digital encoding, display or transmission become the image's structure and material.

sources.title: Rosa Menkman — A Vernacular of File Formats

styles.name: Datamoshing
styles.description: Video-compression structures are disrupted so that movement carries fragments and colors from one frame into another.

sources.title: Carolyn L. Kane — Chroma Glitch: Data as Style

styles.name: Databending
styles.description: Image data is interpreted or altered through unintended processes, producing ruptured colors, bands and unpredictable structures.

sources.title: Rosa Menkman — A Vernacular of File Formats

styles.name: Pixel Sorting
styles.description: Pixels are reordered by visual properties, stretching image areas into organized streaks while retaining traces of the source.

styles.name: Slit-scan Imagery
styles.description: Narrow slices captured at different moments are assembled into one image, stretching movement into continuous ribbons and warped forms.

styles.name: Video Feedback
styles.description: Repeatedly feeding an image back into itself creates recursive tunnels, trails and layered patterns that accumulate over time.

styles.name: VHS Texture
styles.description: Tracking bands, color bleed and unstable tape-like noise give images the worn appearance of analog video playback.

sources.title: Roulette — VX Bliss: Audiovisual Arrangements by Ginny Benson

styles.name: Chromatic Aberration
styles.description: Color channels separate around edges, creating optical fringes that make an image feel refracted, unstable or lens-mediated.

sources.title: V3KTR — optical channel separation and pixel sorting

styles.name: Thermographic Graphics
styles.description: False-color tonal bands replace natural color, turning bodies and objects into vivid fields that resemble heat or scientific imaging.

styles.name: Flow-field Art
styles.description: Many small paths follow a shared directional field, building flowing, hair-like compositions from accumulated motion.

sources.title: The Coding Train — Perlin Noise Flow Field

styles.name: Reaction-diffusion Patterns
styles.description: Simulated chemical interactions generate organic spots and maze-like bands that resemble naturally grown surface markings.

styles.name: Cellular Automata
styles.description: Simple local rules update a grid of cells, creating intricate patterns from repeated small decisions.

sources.title: The Coding Train — Wolfram cellular automata

styles.name: Voronoi Tessellation
styles.description: Space divides into cells around scattered points, producing clustered mosaics with an organic but precise geometric structure.

sources.title: The Coding Train — Weighted Voronoi Stippling

styles.name: Truchet Patterns
styles.description: Repeated tiles rotate and combine into continuous curved paths or networks, creating complexity from a small visual vocabulary.

sources.title: Brad Osgood — Generative art using Truchet tiles

styles.name: Moiré Patterns
styles.description: Overlapping repeated grids or lines create larger interference bands that appear to shift independently of their underlying marks.

styles.name: L-system Graphics
styles.description: Recursively rewritten drawing instructions generate branching structures with the visual rhythm of plants and other growing systems.

styles.name: Fractal Graphics
styles.description: Repeated forms recur at progressively smaller scales, producing intricate images with persistent self-similar structure.

styles.name: Strange-attractor Art
styles.description: Traced trajectories form dense looping structures whose apparent order emerges from a chaotic mathematical system.

styles.name: Particle-field Graphics
styles.description: Large numbers of moving points collectively describe surfaces, currents and shapes that remain visibly particulate.

styles.name: Flocking Graphics
styles.description: Many small agents align, separate and gather into coordinated streams, making collective behavior the primary visual subject.

styles.name: Fluid-simulation Graphics
styles.description: Simulated currents stretch and fold color into swirling plumes, giving digital imagery the behavior of liquid or smoke.

styles.name: Metaball Graphics
styles.description: Soft fields merge into continuous rounded shapes, producing elastic forms that appear to fuse and separate like liquid.

styles.name: Plotter Art
styles.description: Continuous or repeated vector paths create drawings whose precision and accumulated marks reveal a rule-based process.

styles.name: Differential-growth Patterns
styles.description: Curves or surfaces expand at different rates, forming tightly packed folds and organic-looking ridges.

styles.name: Diffusion-limited Aggregation
styles.description: Randomly moving particles gather around a seed to create branching clusters reminiscent of crystals, frost and mineral growth.

styles.name: Lissajous Figures
styles.description: Combined oscillations trace smooth looping curves whose changing ratios produce balanced and intricate geometric forms.

sources.title: The Coding Train — Lissajous Curve Table

styles.name: Topographic Graphics
styles.description: Nested contour lines describe imaginary or real changes in elevation, turning a surface into a flowing diagram of depth.

styles.name: Kinetic Typography
styles.description: Type moves, rotates or changes scale as part of the composition, using timing and rhythm to organize visual attention.

styles.name: Distorted Typography
styles.description: Letterforms stretch, ripple and warp while remaining recognizable, treating text as a flexible visual material.

sources.title: Codrops — Text Distortion Effects using Blotter.js

styles.name: Motion-trail Graphics
styles.description: Repeated afterimages make a moving shape or word leave a visible path, translating time into layered spatial rhythm.

styles.name: Aurora Graphics
styles.description: Soft luminous bands drift across a field, producing a diffuse atmosphere of changing light rather than discrete shapes.

styles.name: Grainy Gradients
styles.description: Fine noise breaks up smooth transitions between colors, giving a luminous digital surface a tactile and atmospheric texture.

sources.title: Codrops — Podium: Grain as a visual language

styles.name: Liquid Distortion
styles.description: Images bend and flow as if seen through moving water, making the surface itself appear unstable and responsive.

styles.name: Particle Typography
styles.description: Many small objects or points assemble into letterforms, so the shape of text remains visible through a particulate structure.

styles.name: Dissolving Typography
styles.description: Letterforms break into dust or fragments, allowing disappearance and dispersal to become part of their visual expression.

sources.title: Codrops — Dissolving Text into Dust and Petals

styles.name: Extruded Typography
styles.description: Visible thickness, perspective and lighting turn letters into sculptural objects that occupy the same space as other three-dimensional forms.

styles.name: Kaleidoscopic Graphics
styles.description: Repeated reflections and radial symmetry transform a small visual fragment into complex rotating fields and ornament.

styles.name: Neo Geo
styles.description: Hard geometric forms and impersonal surfaces evoke circuits, systems, and the organization of commercial life.
styles.distinction: The 1980s conceptual movement uses geometry critically; it is not a label for all geometric abstraction.

styles.name: Arts and Crafts
styles.description: Interlaced botanical ornament, crafted lettering, and integrated page borders celebrate the visible work of making.
styles.distinction: Its craft ethic and ornamental page construction differ from Art Nouveau's flowing modern line.

sources.title: V&A — Arts and Crafts: an introduction

styles.name: Plakatstil
styles.description: A sharply simplified object, a flat background, and bold lettering deliver an immediate visual message.
styles.distinction: The object-led reduction of Sachplakat differs from Swiss Style's extended information grids.

sources.title: National Museum of Modern Art, Kyoto — Modern German Posters

styles.name: Afrofuturism
styles.description: Cosmic imagery, speculative technology, and references to African diaspora histories envision liberated Black futures.
styles.distinction: A cultural and artistic framework centered on Black agency, not a single palette or interchangeable futuristic motif.

styles.name: Impressionism
styles.description: Broken touches of color and soft shifting edges capture momentary light and everyday atmosphere.
styles.distinction: Observed light and fleeting perception distinguish it from the non-naturalistic color of Fauvism.

styles.name: Post-Internet Aesthetic
styles.description: Digital gradients, altered documentation, borrowed online imagery, and physical media artifacts circulate between screen and object.
styles.distinction: Concerns art made within pervasive network culture; unlike Net Art, the work need not exist only online.

styles.name: New Aesthetic
styles.description: Machine vision, mapping artifacts, pixels, and computational patterns reveal digital perception inside ordinary physical life.
styles.distinction: James Bridle's research project concerns how machines see the world, rather than any generic futuristic appearance.

styles.name: Art Brut
styles.description: Personal symbols, unconventional figures, dense marks, and idiosyncratic construction emerge outside academic artistic conventions.
styles.distinction: A category associated with independent, self-taught creation; roughness alone does not make a work Art Brut.

styles.name: Surrealism
styles.description: Dream logic, impossible combinations, transformed objects, and unexpected scale challenge ordinary perception.
styles.distinction: A historical movement exploring the unconscious, distinct from Pop Surrealism's later cartoon and popular-culture vocabulary.

styles.name: Cubism
styles.description: Fragmented planes and overlapping viewpoints reconstruct objects as a compact field of shapes.
styles.distinction: Simultaneous viewpoints distinguish Cubist construction from decorative geometric abstraction.

styles.name: Fauvism
styles.description: Intense non-naturalistic color, simplified forms, and assertive brushwork make color the main organizing force.
styles.distinction: The expressive use of arbitrary color differs from Impressionism's effort to observe changing natural light.

styles.name: Art Nouveau
styles.description: Organic line, botanical forms, and decorative letterforms create a flowing, ornamental visual language.

sources.title: An Introduction to the History of Graphic Design

styles.name: Art Deco
styles.description: Geometric symmetry, stepped forms, streamlined ornament, and polished contrast evoke machine-age glamour.

styles.name: Polish School of Graphic Design
styles.description: Metaphorical imagery, expressive lettering, painterly color, and surreal visual compression.
referenceQueries: Polish School of Graphic Design design
Polish School of Graphic Design aesthetics

styles.name: Japanese Modernism
styles.description: Distilled symbols, precise typography, asymmetry, and generous open space.

styles.name: Soviet Constructivism
styles.description: Geometric forms, photomontage, diagonal energy, and utilitarian communication.

sources.title: An Introduction to the History of Graphic Design

styles.name: Bauhaus
styles.description: Functional geometry, primary colors, clear typography, and reduced forms.

sources.title: An Introduction to the History of Graphic Design

styles.name: De Stijl
styles.description: Rectilinear geometry, primary colors, and disciplined horizontal and vertical structure.

sources.title: An Introduction to the History of Graphic Design

styles.name: Psychedelic Graphics
styles.description: Vibrating outlines, dense ornament, fluid lettering, and saturated color.

styles.name: Punk Graphic Design
styles.description: Cut-and-paste textures, defiant typography, rough reproduction, and stark contrast.

sources.title: An Introduction to the History of Graphic Design

styles.name: New Wave Graphics
styles.description: Layered grids, fragmented typography, sharp color, and playful visual disruption.

sources.title: Design History: The New Wave of Graphic Design

styles.name: Memphis Design
styles.description: Playful geometry, squiggles, pattern clashes, and bright, pastel, or primary palettes.

styles.name: Pop Art
styles.description: Mass-media imagery, bold outlines, repetition, and commercial color.

styles.name: Dada
styles.description: Chance composition, collage, absurd juxtapositions, and anti-rational expression.

styles.name: Futurism
styles.description: Directional motion, dynamic diagonals, machine energy, and fragmented rhythm.

styles.name: Suprematism
styles.description: Floating geometric forms, pure color fields, and non-representational composition.

styles.name: Vorticism
styles.description: Angular abstraction, compressed movement, and industrial energy.

styles.name: Orphism
styles.description: Rhythmic circles, luminous color, and musical abstraction.

styles.name: Rayonism
styles.description: Intersecting rays and translucent planes suggest motion and fractured light.

styles.name: Precisionism
styles.description: Crisp industrial forms, simplified urban geometry, and clean edges.

styles.name: Op Art
styles.description: Optical patterns and calculated contrast create perceptual movement.

styles.name: Kinetic Art
styles.description: Repeated forms and visual rhythm imply or produce movement.

styles.name: Abstract Expressionism
styles.description: Gestural marks, open composition, and emotionally charged color.

styles.name: Hard-Edge Abstraction
styles.description: Flat color planes with sharply defined boundaries and little visible brushwork.

styles.name: Color-Field Painting
styles.description: Broad expanses of color create quiet, immersive compositions.

styles.name: Lyrical Abstraction
styles.description: Fluid marks, intuitive gestures, and flowing color relationships.

styles.name: Neo-Expressionism
styles.description: Raw imagery, assertive mark-making, and clashing or intense color.

styles.name: Pop Surrealism
styles.description: Polished fantasy imagery combines whimsical, uncanny, and pop-cultural motifs.

styles.name: Fluxus Graphics
styles.description: Playful instructions, everyday objects, and anti-hierarchical presentation.

styles.name: Situationist Graphics
styles.description: Détourned mass imagery and disrupted commercial signs carry critical intent.

styles.name: Postmodern Graphic Design
styles.description: Historical quotation, layered references, and playful typography.

sources.title: An Introduction to the History of Graphic Design

styles.name: Flat-vector illustration
styles.description: Crisp filled shapes and limited shading create a clean digital image.

styles.name: Minimal line illustration
styles.description: Sparse contours suggest form with very few marks.

styles.name: Doodle illustration
styles.description: Casual drawn marks and simplified figures feel spontaneous.

styles.name: Conceptual editorial illustration
styles.description: A metaphorical image makes an abstract subject immediately legible.

styles.name: Anime visual style
styles.description: Stylized characters, expressive eyes, and graphic color shape Japanese animation.

styles.name: Manga visual style
styles.description: Sequential storytelling, varied linework, and expressive character shorthand.

styles.name: Chibi illustration
styles.description: Small bodies and oversized heads exaggerate cute character expression.

styles.name: Superflat illustration
styles.description: Flat space and bold outlines connect pop imagery with graphic painting.

styles.name: Kawaii illustration
styles.description: Rounded forms, simplified faces, and sweet color express cuteness.

styles.name: Ligne claire illustration
styles.description: Clean outlines, flat color, and legible comic staging.

styles.name: American comic-book art
styles.description: Dynamic anatomy, ink contours, and sequential action.

styles.name: Mid-century modern illustration
styles.description: Simplified shapes, limited palettes, and playful retro figures.

styles.name: Airbrush illustration
styles.description: Smooth gradients and seamless blending create glossy, dreamlike surfaces.

styles.name: Textured-vector illustration
styles.description: Clean vector forms gain grain, paper, or brush texture.

styles.name: Paper-cut illustration
styles.description: Layered silhouettes and cast shadows imitate cut and stacked paper.

styles.name: Halftone illustration
styles.description: Dots and screens create tonal pattern and print-like texture.

styles.name: Crosshatch drawing
styles.description: Intersecting lines model shadow, volume, and texture.

styles.name: Stipple illustration
styles.description: Dots of varying density create tone and detail.

styles.name: Scratchboard illustration
styles.description: Scraped highlights cut through dark surfaces to define form.

styles.name: Charcoal illustration
styles.description: Smudged dark masses and soft marks create dramatic tonal range.

styles.name: Colored-pencil illustration
styles.description: Layered strokes and visible pigment give drawings a tactile finish.

styles.name: Marker illustration
styles.description: Broad saturated strokes create clean, fast, graphic color.

styles.name: Screenprint aesthetic
styles.description: Flat ink layers, visible overlaps, and constrained color separations.

styles.name: Risograph print aesthetic
styles.description: Grain, vivid spot colors, and slight registration shifts.

styles.name: Letterpress aesthetic
styles.description: Pressed type, raised ink, and textured paper.

styles.name: Woodcut print aesthetic
styles.description: Carved contours and bold light-dark contrast.

styles.name: Linocut print aesthetic
styles.description: Smooth cut marks and simplified relief shapes.

styles.name: Etching print aesthetic
styles.description: Fine incised lines and crosshatching build tonal depth.

styles.name: Lithographic print aesthetic
styles.description: Crayon-like marks and tonal washes transfer to paper.

styles.name: Monotype print aesthetic
styles.description: Singular, painterly impressions retain chance marks.

styles.name: Cyanotype aesthetic
styles.description: Prussian-blue imagery and white silhouettes create a distinctive print.

styles.name: Photogram aesthetic
styles.description: Objects placed on light-sensitive paper create direct shadows and shapes.

styles.name: Paper-ephemera collage
styles.description: Tickets, labels, letters, and found scraps form an archival image.

styles.name: Xerox copy-art
styles.description: High-contrast photocopy marks, noise, and repeated generations.

styles.name: Zine aesthetic
styles.description: Handmade layout, photocopy grain, and direct personal voice.

styles.name: Stencil aesthetic
styles.description: Repeated cut shapes and overspray create a street-print look.

styles.name: Paste-up aesthetic
styles.description: Layered paper images and torn edges suggest public wall culture.

styles.name: Decoupage aesthetic
styles.description: Decorative cutouts cover objects or surfaces in layered motifs.

styles.name: Mixed-media assemblage
styles.description: Found materials and image fragments are physically combined.

styles.name: Ink-wash aesthetic
styles.description: Fluid diluted ink and dry-brush marks balance softness and precision.

styles.name: Gouache aesthetic
styles.description: Opaque, matte color and crisp edges create a hand-painted illustration.

styles.name: Watercolor-wash aesthetic
styles.description: Transparent pigments and flowing edges produce a light surface.

styles.name: Impasto painting
styles.description: Thick paint ridges and saturated strokes make texture visible.

styles.name: Pastel drawing
styles.description: Powdery color and soft blending produce luminous, velvety surfaces.

styles.name: Fresco-mural aesthetic
styles.description: Broad matte color and simplified forms suit large public images.

styles.name: Embroidery illustration
styles.description: Stitches form contours, fills, and decorative image details.

styles.name: Quilted-collage aesthetic
styles.description: Fabric blocks and seams organize image, color, and pattern.

styles.name: Beadwork graphic aesthetic
styles.description: Tiny repeated units create ornamental motifs and sparkling surfaces.

styles.name: Tapestry-inspired graphic style
styles.description: Woven pattern, flattened scenes, and decorative borders.

styles.name: Mosaic illustration
styles.description: Small repeated pieces build figures, icons, or patterned fields.
